facts.quote: The move to Opus 5.5, at low effort, cut the benchmark's cost by about 18%. Running prompt-audit cut it by a further 9%, to about 25% below the Opus 4.8 starting point.
facts.note: RELATIVE cost of an internal customer support benchmark (44 tickets) against Opus 4.8: about 18% lower with the move to Opus 5.5 at low effort, about 25% lower after the prompt-audit tool; no money amount, no tokens, no quality given; the cost base (per ticket, per benchmark) is not written

facts.quote: You may have seen that Opus 5.5 costs 40% less to run than Opus 5. That's our estimate for typical workloads billed by token, at default settings. It assumes Opus 5.5 uses fewer tokens per task at its medium default
You may have seen that Opus 5.5 costs 40% less to run than Opus 5. That's our estimate for typical workloads billed by token, at default settings.
facts.note: an ESTIMATE ("our estimate for typical workloads billed by token, at default settings"), not a measurement; relative to Opus 5; the post says it is "not a 40% cut to the price of a token": token prices are 20% lower for input and output and 60% lower for cache reads

facts.quote: Our examples use Opus 5.5 API list prices: $4 per million input tokens, $20 per million output tokens and $0.20 per million cache reads.
